https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.title: IQPPRMxx Configuration Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.description: Schema for IQPPRMxx parmlib member - PCIe-related parameters for managing zEDC Express feature. Note: On z15 and above processors, tunable options are no longer available and will be rejected with message IQP062I, but syntax remains valid for backward compatibility. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=sys1parmlib-iqpprmxx-pcie-related-parameters

zedc_statements.description: ZEDC statement specifying parameters for managing application requests that use the zEDC Express feature

minimum_request_size_to_compress.description: (DEFMINREQSIZE) Minimum size in kilobytes of data to be compressed for request to be eligible for hardware compression. If request size is less than this value, software compression is used instead. Default: 4 KB (z14 and below) or 1 KB (z15 and above). Can be changed dynamically via SET IQP command.

minimum_request_size_to_decompress.description: (INFMINREQSIZE) Minimum size in kilobytes of data to be decompressed for request to be eligible for hardware decompression. If request size is less than this value, software decompression is used instead. Default: 16 KB (z14 and below) or 1 KB (z15 and above). Can be changed dynamically via SET IQP command.

maximum_segments.description: (MAXSEGMENTS) Maximum number of 16 MB storage segments to allocate for problem state compression and decompression requests. Value of 0 disables zEDC Express feature. Values 1-3 are invalid. Default: 4 (64 MB total). Can only be increased dynamically via SET IQP command (cannot be decreased).

oneOf.description: Disable zEDC Express feature - problem state programs will not use hardware compression/decompression
Number of 16 MB segments (4-64 = 64 MB to 1 GB total storage)

al_version.description: (ALVERSION) Specifies whether AL tapes are created that use Version 3 or Version 4 standards.

tape_compact_format.description: (COMPACT) Specifies whether the compact tape format is enabled.

copy_system_default_block.description: (COPYSDB) Specifies the default block size for copy operations.

ddrswap_size_limit.description: (DDRSIZELIM) Specifies the size limit for DDR swap operations.

zhpf_format_writes.description: (HPF_FMTWRITE) Enables or disables zHPF Format Writes support.

zhpf_imbedded_locate_record.description: (HPF_IMBEDDEDLR) Enables or disables zHPF Imbedded Locate Record support.

zhpf_tca_extension.description: (HPF_TTEDCW) Enables or disables zHPF TCA Extension support.

message_aom496i.description: (AOM496I) Enables or disables AOM496I message processing.

pprc_multi_target.description: (PPRCMT) Enables or disables PPRC multi-target support.

pprc_summary.description: (PPRCSUM) Enables or disables PPRC summary reporting.

refresh_ucb.description: (REFUCB) Enables or disables UCB refresh functionality.

refucb_fail.description: (REFUCB_FAIL) Specifies action to be taken when REFUCB fails to update the UCB.

refresh_vtoc.description: (REFVTOC) Enables or disables VTOC refresh functionality.

smf98_dataset_activity.description: (SMF98_DATASET_ACTIVITY) Enables or disables the generation of SMF type 98 subtype 5, 6, 7 and 8 records.

secondary_space_reduction.description: (SSR) Enables or disables secondary space reduction.

suppress_smf19_dump_condition.description: (SUPPR_SMF19_DUMPCOND) Enables or disables SMF19 dump condition suppression.

zero_directory_pds.description: (ZERO_DIR_PDS) Enables or disables zero directory PDS processing.

vtoc_use_zhpf.description: (VTOC_USE_ZHPF) Enables or disables VTOC zHPF usage.

enforce_dc_media.description: (ENFORCE_DC_MEDIA) Specifies enforcement of data class media types.

erase_on_scratch_v2.description: (EOSV2) Enables or disables erase on scratch version 2.

easy_tier_hints.description: (EASYTIERHINTS) Enables or disables Easy Tier hints.

flashcopy_to_global_mirror.description: (FLASHCOPYTOGM) Enables or disables FlashCopy to Global Mirror.

flashcopy_to_xrc.description: (FLASHCOPYTOXRC) Enables or disables FlashCopy to XRC support.

greater_253.description: (GREATER_253) Enables or disables greater than 253 support.

ickdsf_no_dataset_exist.description: (ICKDSF_NODSEXIST) Specifies ICKDSF behavior when no dataset exists.

ickdsf_verify_offline.description: (ICKDSF_VERIFYOFFLINE) Enables or disables ICKDSF offline verification.

jes3_alloc_assist.description: (JES3_ALLOC_ASSIST) Enables or disables JES3 allocation assistance.

number_of_lreccw_per_eos_channel_program.description: (LRECCW_PER_EOSCP) Specifies number of LRECCW per EOS channel program.

mtl_env_wo_dataclass_worm_is_ok.description: (MTL_NO_DC_WORM_OK) Specifies if MTL environment without data class WORM is acceptable.

multi_incremental_flashcopy.description: (MULTINCRFLC) Enables or disables multi-incremental FlashCopy support.

non_vsam_xtiot.description: (NON_VSAM_XTIOT) Enables or disables non-VSAM XTIOT support.

open_close_eov_abend.description: (OCE_ABEND_DESCRIPTION) Enables or disables open/close EOV abend processing.

pprc_sym_config.description: (PPRCSYMCONFG) Enables or disables PPRC symmetric configuration.

cvaf_stat011_preserve_index.description: (STAT011_PRESERVE_INDEX) Enables or disables CVAF STAT011 index preservation.

retry_cvaf_status.description: (RETRY(STAT011)) Specifies RETRY parameter for CVAF STAT011.

tape_auth_dsn.description: (TAPEAUTHDSN) Enables or disables tape authorization by dataset name.

tape_auth_f1.description: (TAPEAUTHF1) Enables or disables tape authorization F1 function.

tape_block_size_limit.description: (TAPEBLKSZLIM) Specifies the maximum tape block size limit.

vol_nsns.description: (VOLNSNS) Enables or disables volume NSNS support.

standard_scratch_category_code.description: (MEDIA1) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3490 standard capacity (CST) scratch category code.

enhanced_scratch_category_code.description: (MEDIA2) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3490 enhanced capacity (ECST) scratch category code.

high_performance_cartridge_tape_scratch_.description: (MEDIA3) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3590 high performance cartridge tape scratch category code.
(MEDIA4) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3590 high performance cartridge tape scratch category code.

enterprise_tape_cartridge_scratch_catego.description: (MEDIA5) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_worm_tape_cartridge_scratch_c.description: (MEDIA6) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise WORM Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_economy_tape_cartridge_scratc.description: (MEDIA7) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Economy Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_economy_worm_tape_cartridge_s.description: (MEDIA8) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Economy WORM Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_extended_tape_cartridge_scrat.description: (MEDIA9) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Extended Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_extended_worm_tape_cartridge_.description: (MEDIA10) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Extended WORM Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_advanced_tape_cartridge_scrat.description: (MEDIA11) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Advanced Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_advanced_worm_tape_cartridge_.description: (MEDIA12) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Advanced WORM Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

enterprise_advanced_economy_tape_cartrid.description: (MEDIA13) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the 3592 Enterprise Advanced Economy Tape Cartridge scratch category code.

error_category_code.description: (ERROR) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the error category code.

private_category_code.description: (PRIVATE) Specifies a 2-byte hexadecimal value to be used as the private category code.

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.title: z/OS Console Configuration
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.description: Configuration for the z/OS console subsystem. Defines individual console devices, system-wide defaults, hardcopy logging settings, and subsystem initialization values. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=sys1parmlib-consolxx-console-configuration-definition

consoles.title: Console Definitions
consoles.description: List of CONSOLE statements, each defining the characteristics of one console. Up to 251 consoles (including the system console) can be defined per CONSOLxx member.

device_number.title: Device Number (DEVNUM)
device_number.description: (DEVNUM) Console device number or console type keyword. Required and must be the first keyword on the CONSOLE statement. Determines which other parameters are valid. Device numbers must match what was specified on the Add Device panel in HCD.

anyOf.description: Console type keyword: SUBSYSTEM (reserved for subsystem use, only AUTH and NAME are valid), SYSCONS (system console attached to this processor), SMCS (SNA MCS console, requires APPLID in INIT), HMCS (Hardware Management Console)
Device number: 1-4 hexadecimal digits, optionally preceded by a slash. Must match the number specified on the HCD Add Device panel.

unit_type.title: Unit Type (UNIT)
unit_type.description: (UNIT) Hardware unit type of the console device. Specify 3270-X for devices that support the 3270 data stream and Read Partition Query. Use PRT for printer consoles. Mutually exclusive with DEVNUM(SMCS) and DEVNUM(HMCS).

name.title: Console Name (NAME)
name.description: (NAME) Console name that uniquely identifies this console across the sysplex. Required for all consoles except the system console. IBM strongly recommends naming the system console. Reserved names that must not be used: HC, INSTREAM, INTERNAL, SYSIOSRS, UNKNOWN, OPERLOG, SYSLOG, LOGON, LOGOFF.

command_authority.title: Command Authority (AUTH)
command_authority.description: (AUTH) Operator command authority level for this console. Determines which MVS operator commands can be entered. IBM strongly recommends using a security product (such as RACF) to control commands instead of AUTH, especially for SMCS consoles. Not valid with UNIT(PRT). The system console is always forced to AUTH(MASTER).

oneOf.description: MASTER: all MVS operator commands; ALL: information, system control, I/O control, and console control commands; INFO: informational commands only
Combination of granular authority levels: SYS (system control + informational), IO (I/O control + informational), CONS (console control + informational)

console_usage_mode.title: Console Usage Mode (USE)
console_usage_mode.description: (USE) How the display console is used. FC defines a full-capability console able to enter commands and receive status displays and messages. MS defines a message stream console (use for printers). SD defines a status display console. SMCS and HMCS consoles only support FC. Not valid with DEVNUM(SYSCONS).

routing_codes.title: Routing Codes (ROUTCODE)
routing_codes.description: (ROUTCODE) Routing codes assigned to this console. Messages with a matching routing code are directed here. Do not assign routing code 11 (programmer information). ALL assigns codes 1-128; NONE assigns no routing codes.

message_levels.title: Message Levels (LEVEL)
message_levels.description: (LEVEL) Message severity levels this console receives. ALL receives every message. Individual levels: R (reply-required), I (immediate action), CE (critical eventual action), E (eventual action), IN (informational), NB (no-broadcast). The system console defaults to ALL,NB.

oneOf.description: Receive all message levels
Combination of message levels: ALL, NB (no-broadcast)
Combination of message levels: R (reply-required), I (immediate action), CE (critical eventual action), E (eventual action), IN (informational)

conversational_mode.title: Conversational Mode (CON)
conversational_mode.description: (CON) Whether this console operates in conversational mode. When true (Y), operators must verify each message deletion manually using the cursor, selector pen, or CONTROL command. When false (N), messages selected for deletion are automatically removed. Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

scroll_segment_lines.title: Scroll Segment Lines (SEG)
scroll_segment_lines.description: (SEG) Number of lines in the message area that are deleted when the operator enters the CONTROL E,SEG command. Minimum 1; maximum is 99 or the number of lines in the message area, whichever is smaller. Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

message_deletion_mode.title: Message Deletion Mode (DEL)
message_deletion_mode.description: (DEL) Message deletion mode for this console. Y: delete when screen is full. R: roll mode - delete a block of lines after the roll interval when the screen is full. RD: roll-deletable mode - same as R but WTORs, system failure messages, and critical action messages roll to the top and remain. W: wrap mode - new messages overlay old messages from the top. N: no automatic deletion, operator must delete manually. Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

roll_line_count.title: Roll Line Count (RNUM)
roll_line_count.description: (RNUM) Maximum number of lines included in one message roll. When the roll interval elapses and the screen is full, up to this many lines are removed in a single roll operation. Minimum 1; maximum is 99 or the number of lines in the message area, whichever is smaller. Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

roll_interval_seconds.title: Roll Interval Seconds (RTME)
roll_interval_seconds.description: (RTME) Number of seconds between message rolls or wraps. When the screen is full and messages are waiting, the system rolls or wraps after this interval. Fractional values 1/2 and 1/4 are supported (except on 3290 devices). Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

oneOf.description: Fractional-second interval (not valid for 3290 devices)

message_display_format.title: Message Display Format (MFORM)
message_display_format.description: (MFORM) Display format of messages on this console. M shows message text only. Combination values add: J (job ID or name), S (originating system name), T (timestamp), X (suppress job/system name for JES3 global-processor messages). Multiple values may be combined. Ignored when DEVNUM(SYSCONS).

oneOf.description: Message text only (no timestamp, job ID, or system name)
Combination of format options: J (job ID/name), S (system name), T (timestamp), X (suppress JES3 global names)

display_areas.title: Display Areas (AREA)
display_areas.description: (AREA) Sizes of out-of-line display areas on the console screen, expressed as line counts per area. The first value defines the bottom area; subsequent values define areas moving toward the top. Minimum 4 lines per area; maximum 11 areas; the total of all area lines must not exceed the screen size. Specify NONE for no out-of-line areas. Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

oneOf.description: No out-of-line display areas
List of area sizes in lines (4-99 per area, up to 11 areas; total must not exceed screen size)

pfk_table_name.title: PFK Table Name (PFKTAB)
pfk_table_name.description: (PFKTAB) Name of the Program Function Key table from a PFKTABxx parmlib member that defines PFK definitions for this console. The named table must be active (identified on the PFK parameter of the INIT statement). If not specified, IBM-supplied default PFK definitions are used. Not valid when UNIT is PRT or DEVNUM is SYSCONS.

event_monitoring.title: Event Monitoring (MONITOR)
event_monitoring.description: (MONITOR) Events this console monitors and reports. Enables display of job start/end notifications, TSO/E session tracking with optional timestamps, and device status information. One or more options may be combined.

status.title: Dataset Status Monitoring (STATUS)
status.description: Display names and volume serial numbers of data sets with dispositions of KEEP, CATLG, or UNCATLG when they are freed.

jobnames.title: Job Name Monitoring (JOBNAMES)
jobnames.description: Display job names when jobs start and end, and include the job name in abnormal-end diagnostic messages. Set to 'timestamps' to also show the time in hh:mm:ss format.

sess.title: TSO/E Session Monitoring (SESS)
sess.description: Display TSO/E user IDs when sessions start and end, and include the user ID in abnormal-end diagnostic messages. Set to 'timestamps' to also show the time in hh:mm:ss format.

message_scope_systems.title: Message Scope Systems (MSCOPE)
message_scope_systems.description: (MSCOPE) Systems in the sysplex from which this console receives unsolicited (non-explicitly-routed) messages. An asterisk (*) represents the system on which this CONSOLE statement is defined. *ALL receives unsolicited messages from every system in the sysplex. The system console defaults to MSCOPE(*).

oneOf.description: Receive unsolicited messages from all systems in the sysplex
List of system names; use * to represent the system where this console is defined

command_target_system.title: Command Target System (CMDSYS)
command_target_system.description: (CMDSYS) System in the sysplex where commands entered on this console are sent for processing. Use * to direct commands to the system where this console is defined. Recommended for SMCS consoles because z/OS Communications Server Generic Resources may place the console on different systems at different times.

command_recall_buffer_size.title: Command Recall Buffer Size (RBUF)
command_recall_buffer_size.description: (RBUF) Number of previously entered commands retrievable on this console by pressing the PA1 key. Set greater than 1 to allow retrieval of multiple commands without retyping. Commands entered through PF keys are not retrievable unless CON(Y) is set (except with RBUF(1)). Range: 1-15.

auto_activate_group.title: Auto-Activate Group (AUTOACT)
auto_activate_group.description: (AUTOACT) Name of the console group (defined in CNGRPxx) used to automatically control whether the system console enters or exits problem determination (PD) mode. When this group is active and not suspended, the system console automatically enters PD mode when all group consoles are inactive, and exits PD mode when any group console becomes active. Only valid when DEVNUM(SYSCONS).

attached_system.title: Attached System (SYSTEM)
attached_system.description: (SYSTEM) Name of the system this console is expected to be physically attached to and activated on. Used primarily for consoles attached to multiple systems and managed by a physical switch. Mutually exclusive with DEVNUM(SMCS) and DEVNUM(HMCS).

logical_unit_name.title: Logical Unit Name (LU)
logical_unit_name.description: (LU) VTAM logical unit name that exclusively uses this SMCS console. When specified, only this LU can activate the console and no other console can use the same LU. Only valid with DEVNUM(SMCS).

logon_requirement.title: Logon Requirement (LOGON)
logon_requirement.description: (LOGON) Operator logon requirement for this console. Overrides the DEFAULT statement LOGON value for this specific console. REQUIRED: operator must log on before issuing commands. OPTIONAL: logon is optional (commands from non-logged-on operators use ID *BYPASS*). AUTO: console automatically logs on using the console name as the user ID when activated. DEFAULT: use the LOGON value from the DEFAULT statement. The system console is always treated as OPTIONAL regardless of this setting. IBM recommends REQUIRED for SMCS consoles.

receive_internal_id_messages.title: Receive Internal ID Messages (INTIDS)
receive_internal_id_messages.description: (INTIDS) Whether this console receives messages directed to console ID zero (the internal console ID). When true (Y), messages addressed to ID zero are delivered here. When false (N), they are not.

receive_unknown_id_messages.title: Receive Unknown ID Messages (UNKNIDS)
receive_unknown_id_messages.description: (UNKNIDS) Whether this console receives messages directed to unknown or unresolvable 1-byte console IDs. When true (Y), messages issued to a now-unresolvable console ID are delivered here. When false (N), they are not.

allow_commands_without_pd_mode.title: Allow Commands Without PD Mode (ALLOWCMD)
allow_commands_without_pd_mode.description: (ALLOWCMD) Whether the system console can issue commands without first entering problem determination (PD) mode. When false (N, default), the system console is restricted from issuing commands until it enters PD mode via VARY CN(*),ACTIVATE. When true (Y), commands are permitted even outside PD mode. Only valid when DEVNUM(SYSCONS).

standby_mode_support.title: Standby Mode Support (SUPSBY)
standby_mode_support.description: (SUPSBY) Whether this console supports standby mode. Valid only with DEVNUM(devnum) USE(FC). HMCS consoles are always true and cannot be changed. When true (Y), the console can be placed in standby mode. When false (N), standby mode is not supported.

inactivity_logoff_minutes.title: Inactivity Logoff Timeout (TIMEOUT)
inactivity_logoff_minutes.description: (TIMEOUT) Minutes of console inactivity before the logged-on operator is automatically logged off. Console input activity (pressing Enter, PFK, PA1, or PA2) resets the timer. 0 means the operator is never automatically logged off. Range: 0-99. When LOGON(AUTO) is in effect and the user ID matches the console name, TIMEOUT is ignored.

allOf.title: SUBSYSTEM console: only AUTH and NAME are valid
allOf.errorMessage: DEVNUM(SUBSYSTEM) consoles may only specify 'name' and 'command_authority'. All other properties are invalid for subsystem-reserved consoles.

allOf.title: SMCS console: UNIT and SYSTEM are not valid
allOf.errorMessage: DEVNUM(SMCS) is mutually exclusive with 'unit_type' and 'attached_system'. Do not specify these properties for SMCS consoles.

allOf.title: HMCS console: UNIT and SYSTEM are not valid
allOf.errorMessage: DEVNUM(HMCS) is mutually exclusive with 'unit_type' and 'attached_system'. Do not specify these properties for HMCS consoles.

allOf.title: SMCS and HMCS consoles: USE(MS) and USE(SD) are not valid
allOf.errorMessage: SMCS and HMCS consoles only support USE(FC). Do not specify 'console_usage_mode' as 'MS' or 'SD' for SMCS or HMCS consoles.

allOf.title: UNIT(PRT): display-only properties are not valid
allOf.errorMessage: UNIT(PRT) printer consoles do not support: command_authority (AUTH), conversational_mode (CON), scroll_segment_lines (SEG), message_deletion_mode (DEL), roll_line_count (RNUM), roll_interval_seconds (RTME), display_areas (AREA), pfk_table_name (PFKTAB).

allOf.title: ALLOWCMD is only valid for DEVNUM(SYSCONS)
AUTOACT is only valid for DEVNUM(SYSCONS)
LU is only valid for DEVNUM(SMCS)
SUPSBY is only valid for MCS device-number consoles with USE(FC)
allOf.errorMessage: 'standby_mode_support' (SUPSBY) is only valid for hex device-number consoles (not SYSCONS, SMCS, HMCS, or SUBSYSTEM) with 'console_usage_mode' set to 'FC'.

allOf.title: SYSCONS: display and screen properties are not valid
allOf.errorMessage: DEVNUM(SYSCONS): the following properties are not valid for the system console and must be removed: unit_type (UNIT), console_usage_mode (USE), conversational_mode (CON), scroll_segment_lines (SEG), message_deletion_mode (DEL), roll_line_count (RNUM), roll_interval_seconds (RTME), display_areas (AREA), pfk_table_name (PFKTAB), standby_mode_support (SUPSBY), attached_system (SYSTEM).

console_defaults.title: Console Defaults
console_defaults.description: DEFAULT statement defining system-wide console defaults for all MCS, HMCS, and SMCS consoles. Applies to individual consoles that specify LOGON(DEFAULT) or that do not override a given parameter. Only one DEFAULT statement is allowed per CONSOLxx member.

routing_codes.title: Default Routing Codes (ROUTCODE)
routing_codes.description: (ROUTCODE) Default routing codes applied to messages that carry no routing information. ALL assigns codes 1-128; NONE assigns none. If ROUTCODE is not coded, routing codes 1-16 are used by default.

logon_requirement.title: Default Logon Requirement (LOGON)
logon_requirement.description: (LOGON) System-wide default logon requirement for MCS, SMCS, and HMCS consoles. Applies to all consoles that specify LOGON(DEFAULT) or that do not include a LOGON parameter on their CONSOLE statement. REQUIRED: operators must log on before issuing commands (except from a master-authority console before a security product is active). OPTIONAL: logon is optional; non-logged-on operators use ID *BYPASS*. AUTO: consoles are automatically logged on using the console name as the user ID when activated. The system console is always treated as OPTIONAL regardless of this setting. IBM recommends REQUIRED for SMCS consoles.

hold_mode_enabled.title: Hold Mode Enabled (HOLDMODE)
hold_mode_enabled.description: (HOLDMODE) Whether hold mode is enabled for consoles in roll, roll-deletable, or wrap mode. When true (YES), operators can press the ENTER key with no input to suspend or resume the flow of messages on the console screen. When false (NO, default), hold mode is not available.

max_reply_id.title: Maximum Reply ID (RMAX)
max_reply_id.description: (RMAX) Maximum value of a WTOR reply ID in the sysplex. Also determines the width of the reply ID field displayed in message text (e.g., RMAX(9999) produces a 4-digit reply ID). Affects the required size of the XCF couple data set. Range: 99-9999.

synchronous_message_group.title: Synchronous Message Group (SYNCHDEST)
synchronous_message_group.description: (SYNCHDEST) Name of the console group (defined in CNGRPxx) that receives synchronous messages - those issued with WTO or WTOR macros specifying SYNCH=YES. The system routes the message to the first available active MCS or HMCS console in the group. Synchronous messages cannot be routed to another sysplex member; they must be answered promptly to avoid SFM removing the system. SMCS consoles in the group are skipped. The reserved name *SYSCON* routes to the system console. If not specified, synchronous messages go to the system console.

hardcopy.title: Hardcopy Configuration
hardcopy.description: HARDCOPY statement defining the hardcopy message set (the messages written to SYSLOG and/or OPERLOG). Establishes the output destination, routing code filter, command inclusion level, and date format for hardcopy records. Only one HARDCOPY statement is allowed per CONSOLxx member.

hardcopy_output.title: Hardcopy Output Destination (DEVNUM)
hardcopy_output.description: (DEVNUM) Hardcopy output destination. SYSLOG directs records to the system log. OPERLOG activates the operations log and directs records there. Both can be active simultaneously in either order. If OPERLOG is specified but the operations log is unusable, the system falls back to SYSLOG.

use_syslog.title: Use SYSLOG
use_syslog.description: Direct hardcopy records to SYSLOG (the system log).

use_operlog.title: Use OPERLOG
use_operlog.description: Activate OPERLOG (the operations log) and direct hardcopy records there. Can be combined with use_syslog.

routing_codes.title: Hardcopy Routing Codes (ROUTCODE)
routing_codes.description: (ROUTCODE) Routing codes used to select messages for the hardcopy message set. At initialization, a minimum set of routing codes (1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 10, 42) is always included regardless of this setting. ALL selects all routing codes 1-128; NONE limits hardcopy to the minimum set only.

command_inclusion_level.title: Command Inclusion Level (CMDLEVEL)
command_inclusion_level.description: (CMDLEVEL) Types of operator commands and system command responses included in the hardcopy message set. NOCMDS: exclude commands and responses unless they meet routing-code criteria (only honoured in single-system sysplexes with one non-display console). INCMDS: include commands and responses, but exclude status displays. STCMDS/CMDS: include commands, responses, and static status displays (the two values are equivalent).

date_format.title: Hardcopy Date Format (HCFORMAT)
date_format.description: (HCFORMAT) Format of the Julian date in SYSLOG and Master Trace hardcopy records. CENTURY uses a 4-digit year (yyyyddd format); review any programs that parse SYSLOG records before switching to CENTURY. YEAR uses a 2-digit year (yyddd format).

initialization.title: Initialization Settings
initialization.description: INIT statement containing system-wide initialization values for the console subsystem. These values govern message buffer limits, active facility configuration, parmlib member references, and system-level parameters. Only one INIT statement is allowed per CONSOLxx member.

wto_buffer_limit.title: WTO Buffer Limit (MLIM)
wto_buffer_limit.description: (MLIM) Maximum number of write-to-operator (WTO) message buffers. Each buffer is 384 bytes obtained from private storage (subpool 229) in the CONSOLE address space. Range: 20-9999.

syslog_buffer_limit.title: SYSLOG Buffer Limit (LOGLIM)
syslog_buffer_limit.description: (LOGLIM) Maximum number of SYSLOG buffers. Each buffer is 156 bytes obtained from extended common service area (ECSA). Ensure sufficient ECSA is available for the value specified. For JES3 systems using DLOG, IBM recommends at least: LOGLIM = 4000 + (2000 x number-of-JES3-locals). Range: 1000-999999.

wtor_buffer_limit.title: WTOR Buffer Limit (RLIM)
wtor_buffer_limit.description: (RLIM) Maximum number of write-to-operator-with-reply (WTOR) message buffers. Each buffer is 104 bytes obtained from ECSA. IBM suggests specifying a value greater than 99. In a multi-system sysplex, the default equals the RMAX value from the first system that joined the sysplex. Range: 5-9999.

action_message_retention.title: Action Message Retention Facility (AMRF)
action_message_retention.description: (AMRF) Whether the Action Message Retention Facility (AMRF) is active. When true (Y, default), the SYSCONS extended MCS console DOM attribute is set to DOM(NORMAL). When false (N), the SYSCONS DOM attribute is set to DOM(ALL) and non-SYSCONS extended EMCS consoles do not receive DOMs.

message_exit_enabled.title: Message Processing Exit Enabled (UEXIT)
message_exit_enabled.description: (UEXIT) Whether the WTO/WTOR installation message-processing exit IEAVMXIT is active. When true (Y, default), IEAVMXIT is activated if it exists in the link library. When false (N), the exit is not called. Note: IBM no longer ships a default IEAVMXIT in SYS1.LINKLIB.

message_processing_facility.title: Message Processing Facility (MPF)
message_processing_facility.description: (MPF) Message Processing Facility activation and configuration. Set to false to disable MPF. Specify one or more 2-character MPFLSTxx parmlib member suffixes to activate MPF with those members concatenated.

oneOf.description: Message processing facility not active
List of MPFLSTxx member suffixes (2-character alphanumeric each); members are concatenated in the order listed

message_translation_service.title: MVS Message Service (MMS)
message_translation_service.description: (MMS) MVS Message Service activation. Set to false (NO) to disable. Specify a 2-character MMSLSTxx parmlib member suffix to activate the service using that member.

pfk_table_suffix.title: PFK Table Suffix (PFK)
pfk_table_suffix.description: (PFK) PFKTABxx parmlib member that defines PFK tables for the consoles. Set to false (NONE) to use IBM-supplied default PFK definitions. Specify a 2-character alphanumeric suffix matching the PFKTABxx member to load. The selected member must also be referenced by PFKTAB on individual CONSOLE statements.

oneOf.description: No PFK tables; use IBM-supplied default PFK definitions
PFKTABxx member suffix (2-character alphanumeric)

console_group_suffixes.title: Console Group Suffixes (CNGRP)
console_group_suffixes.description: (CNGRP) CNGRPxx parmlib members that define console groups for this system or sysplex. Set to false (NO) to activate no console group definitions. Specify up to 38 two-character alphanumeric suffixes identifying CNGRPxx members to load.

oneOf.description: No console group definitions activated
List of CNGRPxx member suffixes (2-character alphanumeric each); up to 38 entries

mount_message_enrichment.title: Mount Message Enrichment (MONITOR)
mount_message_enrichment.description: (MONITOR) Additional status information to include in mount messages displayed on consoles. When enabled, the system can append volume space availability and/or the name of the first non-temporary data set allocated on the volume to mount messages.

space.title: Volume Space Display (SPACE)
space.description: (SPACE) Display available space on the direct access volume in mount messages.

dataset_name.title: Dataset Name Display (DSNAME)
dataset_name.description: (DSNAME) Display the name of the first non-temporary data set allocated on the volume in mount messages. Data sets with a disposition of delete do not appear.

command_delimiter.title: Command Delimiter (CMDDELIM)
command_delimiter.description: (CMDDELIM) Single character that MCS, SMCS, and HMCS operators use to separate multiple commands entered on one console input line. Each command separated by the delimiter is processed independently. PF keys always use semicolon (;) as the delimiter regardless of this setting. Choose carefully: % and ? conflict with SLIP indirect addressing; ; conflicts with OLTEP; & conflicts with system symbols; : conflicts with SETIOS TIME. Not recognised from Subsystem (SS) consoles.

component_trace_member.title: Component Trace Member (CTRACE)
component_trace_member.description: (CTRACE) Name of the parmlib member containing tracing options for the Operations Services (OPS) component. Must follow the format CTnOPSxx, where n is an alphanumeric source identifier (IBM-supplied members use 'I') and xx is a 2-character suffix.

route_response_timeout_seconds.title: Route Response Timeout (ROUTTIME)
route_response_timeout_seconds.description: (ROUTTIME) Maximum seconds the ROUTE *ALL, ROUTE *OTHER, or ROUTE systemgroupname command waits for responses from each system before aggregating them. The value set on the first system that joins the sysplex applies to all subsequent members unless overridden with a CONTROL M command. 0 disables aggregation and sends each system's response separately back to the ROUTE command originator. Range: 0-999.

smcs_applid.title: SMCS VTAM Application ID (APPLID)
smcs_applid.description: (APPLID) z/OS Communications Server VTAM APPLID for SMCS on this system. Each system in the sysplex must have a unique APPLID. If not specified, SMCS is unavailable for the life of the system. Required before SMCS or HMCS console definitions are used.

smcs_generic_resource.title: SMCS Generic Resource Name (GENERIC)
smcs_generic_resource.description: (GENERIC) z/OS Communications Server Generic Resource name for SMCS in the sysplex. The first system to IPL with this set establishes the GENERIC name for the sysplex lifetime (unless changed via CONTROL M). Requires APPLID to also be specified. Prerequisites: z/OS Communications Server must be an APPN node, the system must be in a sysplex (not a monoplex), a Coupling Facility must be available, and the ISTGENERIC structure must be defined in the CF policy.

message_flood_control.title: Message Flood Control (MSGFLD)
message_flood_control.description: (MSGFLD) Message Flood Automation policy configuration. Specifies the MSGFLDxx parmlib member to load during system initialization and whether the policy should be automatically enabled on load.

member.title: MSGFLDxx Member Suffix
member.description: MSGFLDxx member suffix to load, or false (NONE) to load no member. When NONE is specified, the built-in policy is used if 'enable' is true.

anyOf.description: No MSGFLDxx member loaded; built-in policy applies if 'enable' is true
MSGFLDxx member suffix (2-character alphanumeric or national characters)

enable.title: Enable on Load
enable.description: Whether Message Flood Automation policy is automatically enabled when the parmlib member is loaded during system initialization. When true (ON), the policy is enabled on load. When false (OFF), it must be enabled manually.

anyOf.description: ALL (routing codes 1-128) or NONE (no routing codes)
List of individual routing codes (1-128) or contiguous ranges

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.title: PFKTAB
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.description: PFKTABxx (program function key table definition) defines one or more program function key (PFK) tables for console configuration. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/3.2.0?topic=sys1parmlib-pfktabxx-program-function-key-table-definition

table_name.description: (TABLE) Name associated with this PFK table. Referenced from CONSOLxx parmlib member as PFKTAB(tablname). https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/3.2.0?topic=definition-statements-parameters-pfktabxx

pfk_definitions.description: Array of program function key definitions for this table. Each key (1-24) can be defined once per table.

key_number.description: The program function key number(s) being defined (1-24). Must be unique within the table.

command.description: (CMD) Command(s) to execute when PFK is pressed. Multiple commands can be specified. Each command maximum 126 characters including quotes. If command contains underscore for cursor placement, conversational must be true.

key_reference.description: (KEY) Associates this PFK with another key or list of keys. When this PFK is pressed, processes the referenced key(s). Cannot reference self. Maximum 62 keys in list.

conversational.description: (CON) Specifies whether the PFK is conversational. True (CON(Y)) - system displays command for modification before execution. False (CON(N)) - system executes command immediately. Required if command contains underscore for cursor placement. Default: false

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.title: IARPRMxx Real Storage Manager Controls Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.description:
Base schema for IARPRMxx parmlib real storage manager controls. 
Source documentation: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=sys1parmlib-iarprmxx-real-storage-manager-controls

dedicated_memory.description:
(DEDICATEDMEMORY, alias: DMEM) Specifies the amount of real memory designated as Dedicated Memory. Documented minimum is 4G, and the value must represent a multiple of 2G. Additional system-managed constraints apply, including retaining at least 16G of online non-dedicated memory and maintaining total configured memory as a multiple of 2G. No default value is defined. 
See: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=controls-statements-parameters-iarprmxx

amount.description: The amount of dedicated memory. Must be at least 4 when unit is G, and must represent a multiple of 2G when converted to gigabytes.

unit.description: The unit of measurement for dedicated memory amount: G for gigabytes or T for terabytes.

prompt.description:
(PROMPT) Controls whether the operator is prompted to continue IPL after the memory configuration is displayed. Set to true for YES and false for NO. The documented default is NO. 
See: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=controls-statements-parameters-iarprmxx

restrict_pftcads.description:
(RESTRICTPFTCADS) Controls access to the Page Frame Table Control Area Data Space (PFTCADS). Set to true for YES so that only the operating system can access PFTCADS, or false for NO to allow application access. The documented default is NO. This control was introduced in z/OS 3.2. 
See: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=controls-statements-parameters-iarprmxx

iarr2v_require_authorization.description:
(IARR2V_REQAUTH) Controls authorization requirements for the IARR2V macro service. Set to true for YES to require authorization for real storage access, or false for NO to allow unauthorized applications to invoke the service for any real storage. When true, requests fail for key 8-15 and problem state applications without the required authorization. The documented default is NO. This control was introduced in z/OS 3.2. 
See: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=controls-statements-parameters-iarprmxx

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.title: IECIOS
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.description: IECIOSxx to control various hardware features. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=sys1parmlib-ieciosxx-io-related-parameters

missing_interrupt_handler.description: (MIH) The MIH detects missing interrupt conditions. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-missing-interrupt-handler-mih

then.description: ERROR: When 'device_number' (DEV) is specified, either 'time' (TIME) or 'io_timing' (IOTIMING) must also be provided. DEV identifies which devices the timing interval applies to, and requires either TIME (for MIH intervals) or IOTIMING (for I/O timing limits) to specify the actual interval value.

ERROR: When 'time' (TIME) is specified, 'device_number' (DEV) must also be provided. The TIME parameter specifies the MIH time interval for specific devices identified by DEV. These parameters must be used together.

ERROR: When 'io_timing' (IOTIMING) is specified, 'device_number' (DEV) must also be provided. The IOTIMING parameter specifies I/O timing limits for specific devices identified by DEV. These parameters must be used together.

ERROR: 'permanent_error_on_hyperswap_timeout' (IOTTERM) is only valid when 'enable_hyperswap_io_timing' (IOTHSWAP) is set to true. IOTTERM controls whether timed-out I/O operations that trigger a HyperSwap are terminated with a permanent error or allowed to start on the swap device. You must enable IOTHSWAP before using IOTTERM.

ERROR: When 'enable_hyperswap_io_timing' (IOTHSWAP) is enabled, you must also specify 'permanent_error_on_hyperswap_timeout' (IOTTERM) to control timeout behavior. IOTTERM determines whether timed-out operations are terminated with permanent errors or allowed to retry on the swap device.

character_reader_interval.description: (CHAR) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the character reader device class, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

communications_interval.description: (COMM) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the communications device class, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

channel_to_channel_interval.description: (CTC) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the channel-to-channel device class, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

direct_access_device_interval.description: (DASD) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for all direct access devices (DASD), where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

device_number.description: (DEV) Specifies the device numbers for which the TIME interval applies.

graphics_device_interval.description: (GRAF) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the graphics device class, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

halt_and_clear_subchannel_interval.description: (HALT) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for monitoring Halt (HSCH) and clear (CSCH) subchannel operations. This keyword is device independent; setting it affects all devices on the system.

non_paging_direct_access_storage_device_.description: (IOTDASD) Specifies the I/O timing limit to be used for all non-paging direct access storage devices (DASD), where mm is minutes and ss is seconds. The maximum I/O timing limit is 5,999 seconds. When IOTDASD is set to 00:00, I/O timing is not in effect for the DASD device class.

enable_hyperswap_io_timing.description: (IOTHSWAP) Specifies whether the I/O timing facility is enabled for HyperSwap.

tape_device_interval.description: (IOTTAPE) Specifies the I/O timing limit to be used for all TAPE devices, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds. The maximum I/O timing limit is 5,999 seconds. When IOTTAPE is set to 00:00, I/O timing is not in effect for the TAPE device class.

permanent_error_on_hyperswap_timeout.description: (IOTTERM) Valid only when IOTHSWAP=YES. Specifies whether a timed out I/O operation that triggers a HyperSwap is terminated with a permanent error or allowed to be started on the swap 'TO' device.

mount_pending_interval.description: (MNTS) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for monitoring mount pending conditions for DASD and TAPE devices.

issue_mount_pending_messages.description: (MOUNTMSG) Specifies that MIH is to issue all MIH mount pending messages.

message_only_recovery.description: (MSGONLY) Specifies whether an I/O timeout condition is processed using full I/O timing recovery (MSGONLY=NO) or message only recovery (MSGONLY=YES). When MSGONLY=NO is specified and an I/O request exceeds the I/O timing interval, a message is issued to the operator, a record is written to SYS1.LOGREC, and the I/O request is abnormally terminated. When MSGONLY=YES is specified and an I/O request exceeds the I/O timing interval, a message is issued to the operator and a record is written to SYS1.LOGREC, however, the I/O request is NOT abnormally terminated. Instead, the request is left in the system. Message-only processing allows the system to detect I/O timeout conditions, but, provides the ability to allow the user to decide which I/O requests should be terminated.

standard_devices_interval.description: (STND) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for all of the following device classes: Character readers (CHAR), Communications (COMM), CTCs (CTC), Graphics (GRAF), Tapes (TAPE), Unit records (UREC), where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

tape_interval.description: (TAPE) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the tape device class, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds. Recommended time intervals by tape device class: 3480 (5 minutes), 3490 (5 minutes), 3490E (10 minutes), 3490E with IBM Enhanced Capacity Cartridge System Tape (20 minutes).

test_MIH_parameters.description: (TEST) Specifies the system is to dynamically test MIH parameters and values. The TEST parameter is ignored during initialization. The system uses this parameter when you issue a SET IOS=xx command to syntax check the MIH updating.

time.description: (TIME) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the devices that are identified on the DEV keyword.

io_timing.description: (IOTIMING) IBM suggests setting your I/O timing limits to 6 seconds or longer

unit_record_interval.description: (UREC) Specifies the MIH time interval to be used for the unit record device class, where mm is minutes and ss is seconds.

hotio_statements.description: (HOTIO) Hot I/O refers to a hardware malfunction that causes repeated, unsolicited I/O interrupts. If such I/O interrupts are not detected, the system can loop or the system queue area (SQA) can be depleted. IOS tries to detect the hot I/O condition and perform recovery before the system requires a reIPL. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-hot-io-hotio

device_threshold.description: (DVTHRSH) Specifies the device threshold for unsolicited I/O interrupts, which must be reached for hot I/O recovery to begin.

non_dasd_non_dynamic_recovery_action.description: (DFLT110) Specifies the device threshold for unsolicited I/O interrupts, which must be reached for hot I/O recovery to begin.

disk_dynamic_non_reserved_recovery_actio.description: (DFLT111) Specifies the recovery action to be taken for a DASD or a dynamic pathing device that is not reserved or assigned.

disk_dynamic_reserved_recovery_action.description: (DFLT112) Specifies the recovery action to be taken for a DASD or a dynamic pathing device that is reserved or assigned.

non_disk_non_dynamic_escon_recovery_acti.description: (SDFT110) Specifies the recovery action to be taken for a non-DASD, non-dynamic pathing device that is attached to an IBM ESCON (or future) channel path.

disk_dynamic_non_reserved_escon_recovery.description: (SDFT111) Specifies the recovery action to be taken for a DASD or a dynamic pathing device that is not reserved or assigned and is attached to an IBM ESCON (or future) channel path.

disk_dynamic_reserved_escon_recovery_act.description: (SDFT112) Specifies the recovery action to be taken for a DASD or a dynamic pathing device that is reserved or assigned and is attached to an IBM ESCON (or future) channel path.

use_boxed_lp_for_all_devices.description:
(BOX_LP) Specifies which device classes should be boxed instead of performing channel path recovery when all of the following conditions are true:
 - The device is defined on the CHPID being recovered.
 - Either all of the device's paths are undergoing recovery or this is the only path to the device.
 - The device is currently reserved or assigned.

The device classes you can specify for BOX_LP are DASD, TAPE, UREC, COMM, CTC, GRAF, and CHAR. You can also specify:
 - false (NONE), to turn off BOX_LP processing for all device classes.
 - true (ALL), to turn on BOX_LP processing for all device classes. ALL is the recommended setting.

oneOf.description: True (ALL) turns on BOX_LP processing for all device classes (recommended). False (NONE) turns off BOX_LP processing for all device classes.
List of device classes to box instead of performing channel path recovery.

terminal.description: (TERMINAL) Specifies special recovery actions for recovering from a terminal or hung interface condition. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-terminal

box_lp.description: (BOX_LP) Specifies which device classes should be boxed instead of performing channel path recovery when all of the following conditions are true: The device is defined on the CHPID being recovered; Either all of the device's paths are undergoing recovery or this is the only path to the device; The device is currently reserved or assigned.

oneOf.description: True (ALL) turns on BOX_LP processing for all device classes (recommended). False (NONE) turns off BOX_LP processing for all device classes.
List of device classes to box instead of performing channel path recovery.

ctrace.description: (CTRACE) Identifies the SYS1.PARMLIB member that contains IOS component trace options. Format: CTnIOSxx where n is an alphanumeric character specifying source (IBM-supplied members use 'I') and xx is any two alphanumeric characters. If not specified, IOS component tracing is activated with minimum operations. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-ctrace

ficon.description: (FICON) Enable or disable switch statistics gathering and fabric I/O priority. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-ficon

stats.description: (STATS) Enable/disable FICON switch statistics gathering. In sysplex environments, consider disabling STATS on all but one system to reduce I/O contention.

fabric_priority.description: (FABRICPRTY) Enable/disable FICON switch fabric I/O priority.

storage.description: (STORAGE) Set storage properties for IOS blocks. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-storage

ios_blocks.description: (IOSBLKS) Specifies if IOS blocks will be obtained in 24 or 31 bit storage.

captucb.description: (CAPTUCB) Enable or disable write protection on captured UCBs. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-captucb

protect.description: (PROTECT) Enable/disable write protection on captured UCBs.

midaw.description: (MIDAW) Enable or disable the MIDAW (Modified Indirect Addressing Word) facility. When disabling with MIDAW=NO, facility remains in effect for one minute to allow queued I/O to finish. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-midaw

hyperpav.description: (HYPERPAV) Indicate whether HyperPAV mode is to be used. Absence of keyword causes no change to system (NO mode on initial IPL). https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-hyperpav

hyperwrite.description: (HYPERWRITE) Enable or disable IBM zHyperWrite data replication. Certain applications (e.g., DB2) can provide their own controls. Should only be used when all synchronously mirrored relationships are managed by HyperSwap. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-hyperwrite

ekm.description: (EKM) Specify encryption key management primary and secondary host names and connection parameters. Requires IOSAS user with OMVS segment. Primary host used exclusively unless failure occurs. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-ekm

primary.description: (PRIMARY) Primary key manager specification. Can be hostname, IPv4 address (ddd.ddd.ddd.ddd), IPv6 address, or NONE. Default port is 3801.

primary_port.description: (PRIPORT) Port number for primary key manager

secondary.description: (SECONDARY) Secondary key manager specification. Can be hostname, IPv4 address (ddd.ddd.ddd.ddd), IPv6 address, or NONE. Default port is 3801.

secondary_port.description: (SECPORT) Port number for primary key manager

max_connections.description: (MAXCONN) Maximum concurrent socket connections to encryption key manager

max_permanent_connections.description: (MAXPCONN) Maximum permanent socket connections to encryption key manager. Must be between 0 and MAXCONN value.

recovery.description: (RECOVERY) Enable or disable certain IOS recovery options. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-recovery

dccf.description: (DCCF) Action for no-paths/intervention-required on paging device. MESSAGE invokes DCCF to issue IOS115A WTOR. WAIT_STATE loads non-restartable wait state X'140'.

dev.description: (DEV) Devices that exploit limited recovery time function. DASD applies to all DASD devices. IOTIMING applies only to devices with IOTIMING facility enabled.

limited_recovery_time.description: (LIMITED_RECTIME) Time in seconds for IOS recovery functions. Range: 2-14 seconds. Value of 0 disables the function.

path_interval.description: (PATH_INTERVAL) Time to monitor channel path errors in minutes. Only valid when path_scope=CU.

path_scope.description: (PATH_SCOPE) Scope of path recovery. CU applies to all devices attached to control unit. DEVICE applies on device-by-device basis.

path_threshold.description: (PATH_THRESHOLD) Minimum path-related errors before action is taken. Only valid when path_scope=CU.

spof.description: (SPOF) Set options for IOSSPOF (Single Point of Failure) system service. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-spof

ignore.description: (IGNORE) Specifies which IOSSPOF service checks to ignore. NONE performs all SPOF checks. PCU and PCUHSWAP are mutually exclusive. Cannot specify NONE with other parameters.

oneOf.description: Perform all SPOF checks
Single SPOF check to ignore
List of SPOF checks to ignore. PCU and PCUHSWAP cannot both be specified.

zhpf.description: (ZHPF) Enable or disable High Performance FICON for IBM z Systems (zHPF) facility. Reserve is done synchronously if ZHPF enabled and device operates in Transport Mode. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-zhpf

zhpf_options.description: (ZHPFOPTS) Set options for High Performance FICON (zHPF) facility. ZHPF may be enabled or disabled when this command is issued. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-zhpfopts

max_size.description: (MAXSIZE) Maximum data transfer size for zHPF I/O requests. Can be 1-1024 megabytes (1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes) or SYSTEM to let system determine based on device and CHPID capabilities. Should only be set at direction of IBM support.

oneOf.description: System determines maximum size based on device and CHPID capabilities
Maximum transfer size in megabytes

read_secondary.description: (READSEC) Enable/disable consistent read from secondary facility. This parameter applies to both ZHPF and ZHYPERLINK.

zhyperlink.description: (ZHYPERLINK or ZHL) Enable or disable zHyperLink facility. Access methods use the read limit to determine I/O candidacy. https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/zos/latest?topic=parameters-zhyperlink

operation.description: (OPER) Enable zHyperLink for operations. ALL enables for all I/O operations. READ enables only for read I/O operations. WRITE enables only for write I/O operations. NONE disables for all I/O operations.

read_limit.description: (READLIMIT) Read data limit in KB. Range: 0-32 KB. 32 bytes are always added to the specified limit. Value of 0 uses system default based on detected capability: Original zHyperLink (4 K + 32) or zHyperLink Acceleration (16 K + 32).

host_name.description: Host name of primary key manager

ipv4_address.description: IPv4 address of primary key manager. Port optionally appended with colon or PRIPORT keyword

oneOf.description: IPv4-mapped IPv6 address of primary key manager
IPv6 address of primary key manager

https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.title: CNGRPxx Console Groups Schema
https://ibm.com/schemas/zosconfig/v0/Har.description: Base schema for CNGRPxx parmlib console group definitions.

groups.description: Console group definitions from CNGRPxx. A member can contain multiple GROUP statements and is limited to 226 lines including comments.

items.description: A console group definition from a GROUP statement.

name.description: (NAME) Console group name. Valid values are 1 to 8 uppercase characters using A-Z, 0-9, #, @, or $. This name must be unique within the CNGRPxx member.

members.description: (MEMBERS) Ordered list of console names in the group. Each console name must be 2 to 8 characters, beginning with A-Z, #, @, or $, followed by A-Z, 0-9, #, @, or $. The reserved value *SYSCON* is also allowed.
